## Get started

1. Download and extract the ZIP into your personal course project.
2. Read the questions and their **Data reference** section. It explains the
   variables, missing-value codes, and supplied file formats.
3. Choose **`midterm-starter.Rmd` or `midterm-starter.qmd`**, enter your name,
   and complete the 14 questions. Use one template, not both.
   Keep the report beside the supplied `data/` folder.
4. Restart R, knit/render the report, and check the resulting HTML before submitting.

The ZIP contains the questions, matching R Markdown and Quarto templates, and
the five required data/verification files. Setup instructions are on this page.

## About the report template

The starter is an **answer-document template**, not a worked solution. It supplies
question headings, R chunks, and routine table/figure formatting. You write the
imports, cleaning, joins, endpoint analysis, plots, checks, and explanations.
Complete the calculations before uncommenting the relevant formatting code.
The questions are the authority for what is assessed; supplied formatting is
not separately graded.

Both the [R Markdown template](files/midterm-starter.Rmd) and
[Quarto template](files/midterm-starter.qmd) are included in the ZIP.
They have the same questions, code chunks, and supplied scaffolding; only the
document-format settings differ. Choose the format you use in class and submit
only one completed template with its HTML.

## What to submit

Submit exactly **two files**:

- Your completed **`.Rmd` or `.qmd` source**.
- Its matching **self-contained HTML report**.

Include all requested code, results, explanations, embedded figures, checksums,
and rendering information. Your source must recreate the image exports using
relative paths. Do not submit separate images, data, CSV/RDS outputs, a README,
a repository link, or a commit SHA.

## Individual-work policy

Course materials and R documentation are permitted. **Collaboration and AI
assistance are not permitted.** See the questions for the partial-credit policy.
